rows.label: What a dollar of SNAP benefits is worth to a household against a dollar of cash
rows.explainer: Most SNAP households spend more on food than their benefit, so the benefit frees cash for other things and is worth nearly its face value (Hoynes and Schanzenbach 2009, American Economic Journal: Applied Economics, find food spending responds to food stamps about as to cash income). 0.95, range 0.85 to 1. Read by every model that values SNAP benefits.

rows.label: Share of SNAP's federal and state cost paid out as benefits
rows.explainer: SNAP's benefits are a little over nine tenths of its federal and state cost; the rest is states' and USDA's administration. 0.92, range 0.85 to 0.97. Read by every model that charges taxpayers for SNAP benefits, so administration is counted the same way.
